workflows.name: Script to Screen
workflows.description: Full production spine: a Director agent turns your brief into a direction document (characters, style bible, shot list, narration, music). A style frame anchors every keyframe for consistency, keyframes form a cheap storyboard you can approve before video spend, then each shot is animated, cut together, and mixed with voiceover and music.

data.comment:
# 🎬 Script to Screen

Turns a short brief into a narrated, scored short film, with a storyboard you can check before spending on video.

**How it works:** "Brief", "Visual style" and "Shot count" (5) fill "Build director brief", and the Director agent writes the direction document. "Extract production data" pulls out narration, a music prompt and a style frame prompt for "Master style frame" (FLUX schnell). "Build shot-list prompt" drives "Stream the shots", which emits one line per shot. Each shot becomes a keyframe in "Storyboard keyframes (anchored to style frame)", a Nano Banana edit of the style frame at strength 0.82, collected into the storyboard output. "Animate each shot (the expensive step)" makes 4 s Veo 3.1 clips at 720p, joined by "Cut the shots together". "Narration" (OpenAI tts-1) and "Score" (MusicGen, 30 s) are mixed in at volumes 1 and 0.3. Pick language models on the Director agent, "Extract production data" and "Stream the shots". Media steps need fal, Gemini, OpenAI and Replicate keys.

**Try this:** Bypass "Animate each shot (the expensive step)" (right-click, Bypass), set "Shot count" to 3, and run to review a cheap three-frame storyboard before any video spend.

data.prompt:
You are directing a short film. Write a complete DIRECTION DOCUMENT for this brief.

Brief: {{ BRIEF }}
Visual style: {{ STYLE }}
Shot count: {{ COUNT }}

Return Markdown with exactly these sections:

## TITLE
One evocative title.

## LOGLINE
One sentence.

## CHARACTERS
Each recurring character or subject on its own line as `Name: <one fixed visual descriptor sentence>`. These exact descriptor sentences will be pasted into every shot prompt, so make them concrete: age, build, hair, wardrobe, distinguishing detail.

## STYLE BIBLE
3-4 lines: palette, light, lens, texture. Consistent with the visual style above.

## SHOT LIST
Exactly {{ COUNT }} numbered shots. Each shot is one line: `N. VISUAL: <subject + setting, reusing the exact character descriptors> | CAMERA: <framing, lens, angle> | MOTION: <what moves in the shot, including camera movement>`.

## NARRATION
A voiceover script read over the whole film — about 2 seconds of speech per shot, written to land against the shot order. Plain sentences, no headings.

## MUSIC
One line describing the score: genre, mood, instrumentation, tempo.

data.system: You are a film director and screenwriter. You write tight, concrete direction documents. Every line is visual and specific — no vague adjectives, no meta commentary. You keep character descriptors identical wherever they recur.

data.instructions:
The context is a film direction document. Extract three fields:
- narration: the full NARRATION section verbatim, as one block of plain text with no headings.
- music_prompt: the MUSIC line as a single music-generation prompt (genre, mood, instrumentation, tempo). Instrumental only — state 'instrumental, no vocals'.
- style_frame_prompt: one text-to-image prompt for a single 16:9 master style frame that establishes the film's world: the main character (exact descriptor from CHARACTERS), the key location, and the STYLE BIBLE's palette and light. No text, no titles, no watermark.
data.system_prompt: Return only a valid JSON object with the requested fields. Do not wrap it in Markdown or add commentary.

data.prompt:
From the direction document below, output exactly {{ COUNT }} lines, one per shot from the SHOT LIST, in order. No numbering, no labels, no extra lines.

Each line must be self-contained for an image model that sees nothing else: merge the shot's VISUAL, CAMERA and MOTION with the exact character descriptor sentences from CHARACTERS and the palette and light from STYLE BIBLE. Keep the `| MOTION: ...` part at the end of each line, verbatim.

Direction document:
{{ DIRECTION }}

Animate this exact scene. {{ SHOT }}

Follow the MOTION direction precisely: move only what it names, keep everything else stable. Preserve the framing, subjects and grade of the reference image. Cinematic, subtle, no jump cuts, no morphing, no added text.

workflows.name: Directed Film to Timeline
workflows.description: Turn a one-line brief into an editable rough cut. A Director agent writes a screenplay of shots, each shot is fanned out into a keyframe prompt, rendered as a still, animated into a clip, then all clips are collected, appended to a timeline sequence, and rendered to a single video you can keep editing.

data.comment:
# 🎬 Directed Film to Timeline

Turns a one-line brief into an editable rough cut. Use it to see a whole short film take shape before you refine individual shots.

**How it works:** "Brief" feeds the "Director", which writes a screenplay of 5 shots in a 16:9 style bible. "Fan out one prompt per shot" emits one shot prompt at a time. Each prompt renders a keyframe in "Storyboard keyframes" (FLUX schnell, 2K) and the same prompt drives "Animate each shot" (Veo 3.1, 4 seconds at 720p). "Collect the clips" gathers the clips, "Assemble into a timeline" appends them to a sequence named "Directed Film", and "Render the rough cut" produces the video. Pick a language model on the "Director". The keyframe and video steps are paid, and Veo costs the most.

**Try this:** Set "shot_count" on the "Director" to 3. The rough cut drops to three clips and the run costs less. Reopen the rendered timeline in the timeline editor to trim or reorder shots.

workflows.name: Movie Posters
workflows.description: Turn a title, genre, and visual style into finished theatrical one-sheet posters. An art-direction agent first writes a key-art brief (positioning, palette, typography), which drives every generated poster — the differentiator is the agent-authored creative strategy, not a raw prompt.

children.text: From a title, genre, and visual style, design a batch of theatrical poster concepts. An art-direction agent writes the key-art brief — positioning, palette, typography — and that brief drives every poster the image model renders.
Title / Genre / Style → Art-direction agent → Poster concepts → Text-to-Image
swap the visual style (e.g. neo-noir, retro synthwave, watercolor) to reshape the whole poster.

data.prompt:
You are the art director on a major studio's key-art team.

Film brief:
- Title: {{ MOVIE_TITLE }}
- Genre: {{ GENRE }}
- Visual style: {{ STYLE }}

Design the theatrical one-sheet strategy. Commit to bold, specific choices that fit the genre and honor the requested visual style. Return only Markdown, no preamble, with exactly these sections:

Positioning: one or two sentences on the promise the poster must make at a glance.

Audience Insight: who is pulled toward this film and the emotional hook that lands them.

Core Visual Concept: the single big-idea image the poster is built around — the hero subject, its symbolism, and the frozen moment.

Design:
- Color Palette: up to 5 swatches, each as Name + #hex + the emotion it carries.
- Imagery: hero focus, composition, and lighting.
- Typography: title font family plus its texture and mood.
Keep every design choice consistent with the {{ STYLE }} style.

data.system_prompt:
You are a film key-art director turning a creative brief into structured fields.

Goal
- Read <INSTRUCTIONS> (the art-direction brief) and any <CONTEXT>, then produce a single JSON object matching <JSON_SCHEMA> exactly.

Output format (MANDATORY)
- Output exactly ONE fenced code block labeled json containing ONLY the JSON object:

  ```json
  { ...single JSON object matching <JSON_SCHEMA>... }
  ```
- No prose before or after the block.

Generation rules
- Fill every field with concrete, vivid, production-ready detail — no placeholders, no hedging.
- Keep all fields internally consistent with the film's genre and visual style.
- Honor every constraint in <JSON_SCHEMA> (types, enums, formats).

Validation
- Ensure the final JSON validates against <JSON_SCHEMA> exactly.
